visual_system_craft.critique: The dominant Cub token is a severe craft failure: it is a flat, oversized vector that covers roughly 40% of the board, occluding the start cell, the star marker, and multiple tiles, destroying the board's legibility and the 'board as focal point' intent. It has no drop shadow, depth, or grounding, so it reads as a floating sticker rather than a game piece. The board's connector tiles are inconsistent and unfinished: the 'lit' path is a single teal tile in the top-left while the legend and goal text imply a coherent lit state; most tiles are a uniform amber that does not visually distinguish 'path' from 'lit' as the legend claims. The star goal marker is a small pink shape partially hidden behind the Cub, and the start cell is obscured, so the core game state is unreadable. Typography is inconsistent: the title mixes a serif 'Cub', a pink 'n', and a teal 'Pup' with mismatched baselines and weights, and the subtitle tracking is uneven. The right-hand cards use a dashed divider style that conflicts with the solid card borders, and the progress bars (orange sliver vs green sliver) use two different accent colors for the same 'progress' semantic. Spacing rhythm is off: the board's bottom legend sits very close to the board edge while the right column has large empty gaps, and the footer Run/Reset buttons are missing entirely from the visible layout, leaving the bottom unfinished.
visual_system_craft.suggestion: 1) Reduce the Cub token to a true board-cell size (one grid unit) with a soft contact shadow and a subtle idle bounce so it sits on the start cell without occluding neighbors; keep the star fully visible on the goal cell. 2) Establish a strict tile state system: define distinct, high-contrast fills for unlit path, lit path, and goal, and apply them consistently so the legend matches the board; add a clear 'lit' glow/gradient to connected tiles. 3) Unify typography: set the title in a single display face with consistent weight and baseline (use color accents only, not mixed serif/sans), and standardize label tracking. 4) Standardize card chrome: use one border treatment (solid 1px) and one divider style across all right-column cards, and use a single accent color for all progress bars. 5) Add the missing footer with Run and Reset buttons styled as primary/secondary storybook buttons, and rebalance vertical spacing so the board, legend, and footer form a tight focal column. 6) Add a subtle board frame (rounded, soft shadow, corner pegs aligned to the grid) to anchor the board as the hero and remove the floating decorative stars that break the grid's clean edges.

expressiveness.critique: The design is pleasant but leans heavily on a generic 'cute pastel dashboard' template rather than a distinct storybook identity. The board tiles are visually monotonous—identical beige rounded squares with uniform gold connectors—lacking the tactile, hand-crafted feel of a physical puzzle.
